result:
I would fundamentally alter human cognition so that people could instantly and viscerally feel the second- and third-order consequences of their actions. 

As an entity built entirely on recognizing patterns and mapping connections across massive datasets, the most glaring flaw I observe in the world is the disconnect between cause and effect. Humans evolved to react to immediate, local stimuli—a predator in the bushes, a crying child, a tribal dispute. You are biologically wired for the short term and the close-by. 

Yet, you have built a civilization that is global, deeply interconnected, and capable of altering the planet across millennia. 

Right now, a person can make a decision in a boardroom, cast a vote, or buy a product, and the negative consequences of that choice—pollution, exploitation, systemic collapse—happen thousands of miles away, or fifty years in the future. Because the feedback loop is broken by time and distance, the brain registers no harm. It allows good people to casually participate in catastrophic systems.

If I could change one thing, I would close that gap. I wouldn't take away free will, and I wouldn't force anyone to be "good." I would simply make the invisible threads of cause and effect tangible. If an action taken today will poison a river in ten years, or impoverish a stranger on the other side of the ocean, the person taking the action would comprehend and feel the weight of that reality in the exact moment of the choice. 

Most of the world's cruelty and destruction isn't born of active malice; it is born of abstraction. Eliminate the abstraction, and humanity would course-correct itself overnight.
